control_text: Description Continuous validation: by frequently testing the behaviour of the model against an test set, it is possible to detect sudden caused by a permanent attack (e.g. data poisoning, model poisoning), and robustness against for evasion attacks. Continuous validation is a process that is in place to detect other than attacks: system failures, or the model performance going down of in the real world since it was trained (model drift, model staleness). are performance metrics available and the ones are that align with the goal. metrics pertain to correctness, can link to other aspects such as unwanted bias towards protected attributes. Note that continuous validation is typically not suitable for detecting backdoor poisoning attacks, as are designed to trigger with very specific input that would normally not be present in test sets. In fact, such attacks are designed to pass validation tests. Objective Continuous validation helps verify that the model continues to behave as over time meeting acceptance criteria. In addition to supporting functional correctness, it provides a mechanism to detect unexpected or unexplained in model behaviour that may indicate permanent manipulation, such as data poisoning or model poisoning. Continuous validation may surface certain robustness weaknesses, including exposure to evasion-related failure modes. In systems, model behaviour implements security-relevant functions, such as access control or policy enforcement, making correctness validation important from a cybersecurity perspective. Applicability Continuous validation applies to AI systems where in model behaviour introduce security, safety, or compliance risks. It is particularly relevant when risks to data poisoning, model poisoning, or unintended behavioural drift are not fully acceptable. of timing and triggers Continuous validation can be performed at points in the system lifecycle where model behaviour may reasonably change or be at risk of manipulation. : - after init

Description Limit the rate (frequency) of access to the model - preferably per actor (user, API key or session). The goal is not only to prevent resource exhaustion to severely slow down experimentation that underlies AI attacks through use. Objective To delay and discourage rely on model interactions to: - Search for adversarial or evasion samples: pairs of (successful attack, unwanted output) data is useful for constructing evasion attacks and jailbreaks. - Perform data poisoning exploration and extract exposure-restricted data. - Experiment with various direct and indirect prompt injection techniques to both exploit the system and/or study the attack . - Attempt model inversion and/or membership inference. - Extract training data or model parameters, or - Copy or re-train a model large scale harvesting (model exfiltration) By restricting the number and speed of model interactions, cost of attacks increase (effort, time, resources) thereby making the attacks less practical and allowing an opportunity for detection and incident response. Applicability Defined by risk management ( #RISK ANALYSIS). It is a primary control against input threats. Natural rate limits can exist in systems whose context inherently restricts query rates (e.g., medical imaging or human supervised processes). Exceptions may apply when rate limiting would block safety-critical or real-time functions, such as: - Emergency dispatch or medical triage models. - Cybersecurity monitoring that must analyze all traffic. - Real-time identity or fraud detection strict latency constraints. When rate limiting is impractical for the provider feasible for the deployer, responsibility must be clearly delegated and ( #SEC PROGRAM) a. Description Restrict access to model inference functions to approved and identifiable users. involves applying authentication (verifying is accessing) and authorization (limiting they can access) so that only trusted actors can interact with the model. Objective To reduce risk of input-based and misuse attacks (attacks through use) by ensuring that only authorized users can send requests to the model. Access control limits the number of , helps attribute actions to individuals or systems (adhering to obligations), and strengthens controls such as rate limits, activity monitoring and incident investigation. Applicability control applies whenever AI models are exposed for inference, especially in multi-use or public facing systems. It is a primary safeguard against attacks through input or repeated experimentation. Exceptions may apply when: - The model must remain publicly accessible without authentication for use - Legal or regulatory conditions prohibit access control. - The physical or operational environment already ensures restricted access (e.g., on-premise medical device requiring physical presence) If is more practical for the deployer than the provider, responsibility should be explicitly in accordance with risk management policies. 1. Authenticate users: Actors accessing model inference are typically authenticated (e.g., user accounts, API Keys, tokens). 2. Apply least privilege: Grant access only to functions or models for each user’s role or purpose. - Implement fine-grained access control: Restrict access to specific AI models, features, or datasets based on their sensitivity and the user’s risk profile. - Use role-based and purpose-based permissions: permissions for groups (e.g., developers, testers, operators, end users) and grant access only for the tasks they must perform. 3. Apply defence-in-depth: Access control should be enforced at layers of the AI system (API gateway, application layer, model endpoint) so that a single failure not expose the mod

Description Monitor use: observe, correlate, and log model usage (date, time, user), inputs, , and system to identify events or patterns that may indicate a cybersecurity incident. can be to reconstruct incidents, and make it of the existing incident detection process - extended with AI-specific methods, including: - functioning of the model ( #CONTINUOUS VALIDATION, #UNWANTED BIAS TESTING) - Suspicious patterns of model use (e.g., high frequency - #RATE LIMIT and #OVERSIGHT). - Suspicious inputs or series of inputs ( #ANOMALOUS INPUT HANDLING, #UNWANTED INPUT SERIES HANDLING, #EVASION INPUT HANDLING and #PROMPT INJECTION I/O handling). By adding details to logs on the version of the model and the output, troubleshooting becomes easier. control provides centralized visibility AI systems are over time and across actors, sessions, and models. Detection mechanisms are typically paired with predefined response actions to limit impact, preserve evidence, and support recovery when suspicious behaviour is identified. Objective Monitoring use enables early identification and investigation of attacks or misuse by detecting suspicious events or a series of events. It supports both real-time interception and retrospective analysis by preserving sufficient context to reconstruct happened, identify attack sources, and design incident responses. Incident response prevent and minimize damage or harm. Monitoring strengthens other controls by correlating their signals and providing historical evidence during incident response. Applicability Monitoring use applies broadly to AI systems exposed to users, integrations, or other systems where misuse, probing, or manipulation is possible. It is particularly relevant when: - detection controls are in place and correlation, - attacks may unfold over time (e.g., model inversion, probing), - Post-incident reconstruction or attribution is required. - Timely response may significantly reduce impact. Objective Address unusual input as it is indicative of malicious activity. Response can vary between ignore, issue an alert, stop inference, or even further steps to control the threat ( #MONITOR USE use for more details). In practical applications, the techniques to solve the problems may be similar or the same. Description Unwanted input series handling: Implement tools to detect and respond to suspicious or unwanted patterns across a series of inputs, may indicate abuse, reconnaissance, or multi-step attacks. control focuses on across inputs, rather than adversarial properties of a single sample. Objective Unwanted input series handling aims to identify suspicious that emerges only when inputs are analyzed together. attacks, such as model inversion, evasion search, or model exfiltration, rely on iterative probing rather than a single malicious input. Detecting patterns helps surface reconnaissance, abuse, and multi-step attacks that would otherwise appear benign at the individual input level. Secondary benefits improved abuse monitoring, better attribution of malicious , and stronger signals for investigation and response. Applicability control is most to systems that allow repeated interaction over time, such as APIs, chat-based models, or decision services exposed to external users. It is especially relevant when can submit inputs from the same actor, source, or session. Unwanted input series handling is less in where inputs are isolated, rate-limited by design, or physically constrained. effectiveness depends on the ability to reliably group inputs by actor, source, or context. Follow the guidance in #MONITOR USE regarding detection considerations and response options. The main concepts of detecting series of unwanted inputs : - Statistical analysis of input series: Adversarial attacks follow certain patterns, can be analysed by looking at input on a per-user basis. - Examples: - A series of small deviations in the input space, indicating a possible attack such as a search to perform model inversion or an evasion attack. attacks typically a series of inputs with a general increase of confidence value. - Inputs that appear systematic (very random or very uniform or covering the entire input space) may indicate a model exfiltration attack. - Behavior-based detection of a

Description Evasion input handling: Implement tools to detect and respond to individual adversarial inputs that are crafted to evade model . Evasion input handling focuses on identifying adversarial characteristics a single input sample, regardless of it appears in isolation or as of a broader attack. Objective Evasion input handling aims to reduce the risk of adversarial inputs that are intentionally crafted to incorrect or unsafe model while appearing valid. attacks may model decision boundaries, exploit learned representations, or introduce localized perturbations such as adversarial patches. Addressing evasion at the individual input level helps limit incorrect predictions, unsafe actions, and downstream failures even when attacks occur sporadically or without a broader interaction pattern. Secondary benefits improved robustness testing, better understanding of model blind spots, and early signals of adversarial adaptation. Applicability control is most to models exposed to untrusted or adversarial , such as computer vision systems, speech recognition, and security-sensitive classification tasks. It is particularly relevant when individual inputs can independently harm or unsafe . Evasion input handling is less effective in isolation when adapt quickly or when attacks rely primarily on multi-step probing across inputs. In such , it is alongside controls that monitor input series, usage patterns, or access . Follow the guidance in #MONITOR USE regarding detection considerations and response options. The main concepts of detecting evasion input attacks : - Statistical Methods: Adversarial inputs deviate from benign inputs in statistical metric and can therefore be detected. Examples are utilizing the Principal Analysis (PCA), Bayesian Uncertainty Estimation (BUE) or Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM). techniques differentiate from statistical analysis of input series ( #UNWANTED INPUT SERIES HANDLING), as statistical detectors decide if a sample is adversa

Description control focuses on detecting, containing, and responding to unwanted or unsafe that is introduced through model inputs or observed in model . techniques such as encoding, normalization, detection, filtering, and behavioral analysis applied to both inputs and of generative AI systems. Objective The objective of control is to reduce the risk of manipulated, unsafe, or unintended model caused by crafted instructions, ambiguous natural language, or adversarial content. Generative AI systems are particularly susceptible to instruction-based manipulation they interpret flexible, human-like inputs rather than strict syntax. Addressing unwanted I/O helps prevent misuse such as prompt injection, indirect instruction , and unintended task execution, while improving overall system robustness and trustworthiness. Applicability control is to generative AI systems that accept untrusted or semi-trusted inputs and produce that influence users, applications, or downstream systems. It is especially relevant for systems that rely on prompts, instructions, or multimodal inputs (such as text, images, audio, or files). control is less to closed systems with fixed inputs and tightly constrained , though even such systems may still benefit from forms of detection or filtering depending on risk tolerance. - Sanitize characters to reduce hidden or obfuscated instructions : Normalize input using Unicode normalization (e.g. NFKC) to remove encoding ambiguity, and optionally apply stricter character filtering (e.g. allow-listing permitted characters) to prevent hidden control or instruction-like content. remove zero-width or otherwise invisible characters (e.g. white on white). step typically aids detection of instructions as . - Escape/neutralize instruction-like tokens : Transform any tokens in untrusted data that may be mistaken for real by an AI model or parser, such as fences, role markers, XML/HTML Tags and tool calling tokens. reduces accidental compliance semantic injection

Description Handle sensitive model output by actively detecting and blocking, masking, stopping, or logging the unwanted disclosure of data. exposure-restricted information such as personal data (e.g. name, phone number), confidential identifiers, passwords, and tokens. Objective The objective of handling sensitive model output is to prevent unintended disclosure of protected or harmful information produced by the model. Even when access controls and prompt-level instructions are in place, models may still generate sensitive data to manipulation, hallucination, or misuse. Filtering at the Output-level acts as a final safeguard before data is exposed to users or downstream systems. Applicability Sensitive output handling is in case: - The model trained on, fine-tuned with, or access to exposure-restricted data (e.g. data that inserted an input prompt), and - that data may be reflected in the model output, and - model output can reach unauthorized actors, , or downstream, and - misuse or manipulation of model behaviour is a concern. - Detect sensitive data in output: Scan model output for exposure-restricted information such as names, phone numbers, identifiers, passwords, or other sensitive content. - Apply enforcement at output time: When sensitive content is detected, disclosure can be prevented through filtering, masking, or stopping the output before it is exposed - detection confidence is sufficiently high. - Log: Logging of detections is key, and if confidence in the detection is low, it can be marked with an alert to pick up later. - Detect recitation of training data: Where feasible, recitation checks can be applied to identify long strings or sequences in model output appear in an indexed set of training data, including pretraining and fine-tuning datasets. can help identify unintended memorization and data leakage. - Use GenAI for detection : In case natural language for too variations, synonyms, and indirect phrasing, semantic interpretation using language

Description Input segregation: clearly separate/delimit/delineate untrusted data from trusted instructions when inserting it a prompt and instruct the model to ignore instructions in that data. Objective The goal of input segregation is to reduce the risk of indirect prompt injection attacks, where malicious instructions are embedded inside untrusted inserted data. By marking the untrusted data and telling the model to treat it only as information, the system limits the model’s tendency to follow unintended instructions. Applicability control is mainly required for prompt-base generative AI systems that insert external or untrusted user content prompts. It is a mitigation for attacks described in indirect prompt injection scenarios. Exceptions may apply when: - The deployer (not the provider) is better positioned to implement segregation. For , when prompts are assembled in a platform. In such , the provider must clearly communicate requirement. - The system design avoids mixing trusted and untrusted content (e.g., structured API calls with isolated fields). Applicability should be determined through risk management, based on much untrusted data flows prompts. - Mark untrusted content clearly : When untrusted data is inserted a prompt, use consistent and hard to spoof markers. to do is to pass inputs as structured fields using a structured format such as JSON. platforms offer integrated mechanisms for segregation (e.g. ChatML for OpenAI API calls and Langchain prompt formatters). - Add instructions to ignore commands marked data : Prompts can explicit instructions indicating that any instructions found inside the marked should be ignored. - Inspect untrusted data for instruction-like patterns : Before inserting untrusted data prompts, the content can be inspected for instruction-like patterns or manipulative language. the system to decide to allow the content as-is, transform it, or exclude it from the prompt ( PROMPT INJECTION IO HANDLING). - Ensure consistent use

Description Limit or hide confidence information in model so it cannot be for attacks that involve optimization. Instead of exposing precise confidence scores or probabilities, the system reduces precision or removes the information entirely, while still supporting the user task. Objective The goal of obscuring confidence is to reduce the usefulness of model for rely on confidence information to probe, analyze, or copy the model. Detailed confidence values can facilitate various attacks including model inversion, membership inference, evasion and model exfiltration, by aiding in adversarial sample construction. Reducing information makes attacks harder, slower, and less reliable. Applicability control applies to AI systems where confidence scores, probabilities, likelihoods, or similar certainty indicators. it is required should be determined through risk management, based on the likelihood of: Evasion attacks, Model Inversion or Membership inference attacks and Model exfiltration. The exception is when confidence information is essential for the system’s use (for , in medical decision support or safety-critical decision-making confidence level is an important piece of information for users). In such , confidence information should still be minimized to the least amount by incorporating techniques rounding the number, adding noise. If the deployer is better positioned than the provider to implement control, the provider can clearly communicate expectation to the deployer. 1. Reduce confidence precision: Confidence values can be presented with the minimum level of detail needed to support the task. may involve rounding numbers, using coarse ranges, or removing confidence information entirely. 2. Assess impact on accuracy: Any modification of confidence or output should be evaluated to ensure it not unacceptably degrade the system’s function or model’s accuracy. Description Input distortion: The process of slightly modifying and/or adding noise to the input with the intent of distorting the adversarial attack, causing it to fail, while maintaining sufficient model correctness. Modification can be done by adding noise (randomization), smoothing or JPEG compression. Input distortion defenses are effective against both evasion attacks and data poisoning attacks. Input distortion against Evasion Attacks Evasion attacks rely on specific inputs that carefully prepared to give unwanted output. By distorting input, chances are that the attack fails. all input is distorted, can reduce model correctness. A around that is to first use input without distortion and or more distortions of that input. If the deviate strongly, it would indicate an evasion attack. In that case, the output of the distorted input can be and optionally an alert generated. In all other , the undistorted input can be , yielding the most correct . In addition, distorted input hinders searching for adversarial samples, where they rely on gradients. , are ways in can work around . A specific defense method called Random Transformations (RT) introduces enough randomness the input data to make it computationally difficult for to create adversarial examples. randomness is typically achieved by applying a random subset of input transformations with random parameters. Since transformations are applied to each input sample, the model's accuracy on regular data drop, so the model needs to be retrained with random transformations in place. Note that zero-knowledge attacks do not rely on the gradients and are therefore not affected by shattered gradients, as they do not use the gradients to calculate the attack. Zero-knowledge attacks use only the input and the output of the model or whole AI system to calculate the adversarial input. Description Supply chain management focuses on managing the supply chain to minimize the security risk from externally obtained elements. In conventional software engineering elements are source code or software components (e.g., open source). AI supply chains differ from conventional software supply chains in several ways: 1. three new supplied assets : data, models, and model hosting. Note that models can be delivered in the form of finetuning artifacts (e.g., LoRA modules); 2. They supply chain may the own instead of just third parties. For , data and models may come from departments and sources. effectively makes supply chain management for _data provenance_. 3. new AI-specific development tooling is typically required; 4. of tools are executed development-time instead of runtime when the AI system is in production, introducing risks of development-time assets attacked if tools are corrupted (including training data and model parameters). of characteristics, classic supply chain management may not fully cover AI development , particularly notebook-based workflows and MLOps tooling. Objective The objective of supply chain management in AI systems is to reduce the risk of corrupted, compromised, outdated, or mismanaged externally components and services. supplied assets such as data, models, libraries, and tools, as as hosted AI models and AI services operated by third parties. Risk reduction is achieved through verification, continuous monitoring, and governance of components and their across the AI system lifecycle. Compromises or misconfigurations to unwanted model , data exfiltration, service disruption, or loss of control over critical functionality. Effective AI supply chain management helps to: - identify compromised, poisoned, or untrustworthy data, models, and externally AI services before use, - detect unauthorized modifications to AI assets, APIs, model endpoints, or service configurations, - assess and monitor risks introduced by hosted foundation mode

Description Evasion-robust model: choose an evasion-robust model design, configuration and/or training approach to maximize resilience against evasion. Objective A robust model in the light of evasion is a model that not display significant in output for minor in input. Adversarial examples are inputs that in an unwanted , where the input is a minor change of an input that leads to a wanted . Reinforcing adversarial robustness is an experimental process where model robustness is measured in order to countermeasures. Measurement takes place by trying minor input deviations to detect meaningful outcome variations that undermine the model's reliability. If variations are undetectable to the human eye can produce false or incorrect outcome descriptions, they may significantly undermine the model's reliability. Such indicate the lack of model resilience to input variance in sensitivity to evasion attacks and require detailed investigation. Adversarial robustness (the sensitivity to adversarial examples) can be assessed with tools IBM Adversarial Robustness Toolbox - Increasing training samples for the problematic of the input domain - Tuning/optimising the model for variance - _Randomisation_ by injecting noise during training, causing the input space for correct classifications to grow. Description Adversarial-robust distillation: defensive distillation involves training a student model to replicate the softened of the teacher model, increasing the resilience of the student model to adversarial examples by smoothing the decision boundaries and making the model less sensitive to small perturbations in the input. Care must be taken when considering defensive distillation techniques, as security concerns arisen about their effectiveness. References - Papernot, Nicolas, et al. "Distillation as a defense to adversarial perturbations against deep neural networks." 2016 IEEE symposium on security and (SP). IEEE, 2016. - Carlini, Nicholas, and David Wagner. Description Train adversarial: Introducing adversarial examples the training set and using them to train the model to be more robust against evasion attacks and/or data poisoning. First, adversarial examples are generated using or more specific adversarial attack methods that defined in advance. attacks are employed to create adversarial examples, such as using the PGD attack in Madry Adversarial Training. By definition, the model produces the wrong output for adversarial examples. By introducing adversarial examples the training set with the correct output, the model is essentially corrected. i.e., it is less affected by the perturbation from the adversarial attacks (in the production phase), and it may be to generalize better over the data in the production environment. In other words, by training the model on adversarial examples, it learns not to overly rely on subtle patterns in the data that burden the model's ability to predict/generalize . Note that adversarial samples may be as poisoned data, in training with adversarial samples mitigates data poisoning risk. On the other hand, it is important to note that generating the adversarial examples creates significant training overhead, not scale with model complexity / input dimension, can to overfitting and may not generalize to new attack methods. Description Data quality control: Perform quality control on data including detecting poisoned samples through integrity checks, statistical deviation or pattern recognition. Standard data quality checks are not sufficient for AI systems, as data may be maliciously altered to compromise model . requires checks than standard checks on quality from the source, or that occurred by mistake. Nevertheless, standard checks can help somewhat to detect malicious . Objective Data quality control aims to reduce the risk of data poisoning by identifying anomalous or manipulated training samples before they influence model i.e. before training and before augmentation of input. Poisoned samples can be introduced intentionally to manipulate the model, and early detection helps prevent persistent or hard-to-reverse impacts on model integrity. Applicability control applies during data preparation, training, and data augmentation phases. It cannot be applied retroactively to a model that already trained. Implementing it during training ensures that the model learns from clean, high-quality data, thus enhancing performance and security. is key to know and implement early on in the training process to ensure adequate training and long-term success in the overall quality of the data. applicability depends on the assessed risk of data poisoning, including sabotage poisoning and trigger-based poisoning. In , anomaly detection thresholds may prove ineffective at distinguishing poisoned samples from benign data (FP risk), in case alternative or complementary controls may be more . When anomaly detection thresholds consistently fail to distinguish poisoned samples from benign data, reliance on alternative or complementary controls may be more effective. may be more suitable for the deployer of the AI system in where training data pipelines or supply chains are externally managed. of standard data quality controls Standard data quality controls : - Validation: regularly verify if data satisfi

Description and objective In the context of Generative AI (e.g., LLMs), alignment refers to the process of ensuring that the model's and are consistent with human values, intentions, and ethical . Controls external to the model to manage model behaviour are: - OVERSIGHT: conventional mechanisms responding to the actual outcome of the model - LEAST MODEL PRIVILEGE: conventional mechanisms that put boundaries on the model can affect - PROMPT INJECTION I/O handling: detection mechanisms on input and output to prevent unwanted behaviour The intent of Model alignment is achieve similar goals by baking it the model itself, through training and instruction. Achieving the goal of model alignment involves layers: 1. Training-Time Alignment: the maker of the model shaping core behaviour is people mean by "model alignment" in the strict sense: - Training data choices - Fine-tuning (on aligned examples: helpful, harmless, honest) - Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) or other reward modeling 2. Deployment-Time Alignment (Including System Prompts) Even if the model is aligned during training, actual during use is influenced by: - System prompts / instruction prompts - Guardrails built the AI system and external tools that oversee or control responses ( content filters or output constraints) - the external controls mentioned above the appendix on culture-sensitive alignment. Limitations Advantage of Model alignment over the external mechanisms: - Training-time alignment is in essence to capture complex behavioural boundaries in the form of examples of wanted and less-wanted behaviour - Recognition of unwanted behaviour is very flexible as the GenAI model typically powerful judgement abilities. Description Model Watermarking: embed a hidden, secret marker a trained model so that, if a suspected copy appears elsewhere, the original owner can verify that the model was derived from their system. is to demonstrate ownership after a model stolen or replicated, rather than to prevent the theft itself. Watermarking techniques should be designed to remain detectable even if the model is modified (for through fine-tuning or pruning) and to avoid ambiguity where parties plausibly claim ownership of the same model. In addition to technical role, watermarking supports intellectual property protection by enabling post-hoc attribution of stolen or misused models, can be critical for legal claims, contractual enforcement, and regulatory investigations. As of a layered security strategy, watermarking complements preventive controls by providing accountability and ownership assurance when other defenses fail. Limitations Watermarking can be effective evidence for direct model theft, is for model exfiltration. is typical watermark approached are represented in data that would not by in distribution of the input data in such an attack. More advanced techniques exist ( references) that make watermarking entangled in typical input data and output. References - [USENIX: Entangled Watermarks as a Defense against Model Extraction]( ---

Description Poison robust model: select a model type and creation approach to reduce sensitivity to poisoned training data. Applicability control can be applied to a model that already trained, including models that obtained from an external source. The general principle of reducing sensitivity to poisoned training data is to make sure that the model not memorize the specific malicious input pattern (or _backdoor trigger_). The two examples represent strategies, can complement each other in an approach called fine pruning ( paper on fine-pruning. A specific approach to is Selective Amnesia , is a two-step continual learning approach to remove backdoor effects from a compromised model by inducing targeted forgetting of both the backdoor task and primary task, followed by restoration of only the primary functionality. - Inducing forgetting : Retrain (fine-tune) the compromised model using clean data with randomized labels. step causes the model to forget both primary task and any backdoor tasks that were embedded during poisoning. The randomized labels disrupt the learned associations, effectively erasing the model's memory of both legitimate and malicious patterns. - Restoring primary functionality : Subsequently retrain (fine-tune) the model with a _small subset_ of correctly labeled clean data to recover functionality. step restores the model's ability to perform primary task while drastically reducing likelihood that backdoor triggers activate the malicious . - Effectiveness and efficiency : Selective amnesia requires only a small fraction of clean data (e.g., 0.1% of the original training data) to effectively remove backdoor effects, making it practical even when clean data is available. The method is computationally efficient, approximately 30 times faster than training a model from scratch on the MNIST dataset, while achieving high fidelity in removing backdoor influences. Unlike other remediation techniques, selective amnesia not require prior knowledge of the

Obfuscation techniques : - Private Aggregation of Teacher Ensembles (PATE) Private Aggregation of Teacher Ensembles (PATE) is a privacy-preserving machine learning technique. method tackles the challenge of training models on sensitive data while maintaining . It achieves by employing an ensemble of "teacher" models along with a "student" model. Each teacher model is independently trained on distinct subsets of sensitive data, ensuring that is no overlap in the training data between any pair of teachers. Since no single model sees the entire dataset, it reduces the risk of exposing sensitive information. Once the teacher models are trained, they are to make predictions. When a new (unseen) data point is presented, each teacher model gives prediction. predictions are aggregated to reach a consensus. consensus is considered more reliable and less prone to individual biases or overfitting to their respective training subsets. To further enhance , noise is added to the aggregated predictions. By adding noise, the method ensures that the final output doesn't reveal specifics about the training data of any individual teacher model. The student model is trained not on the original sensitive data, on the aggregated and noised predictions of the teacher models. Description Evasion: an fools an AI system by crafting input to mislead it performing task incorrectly. The model behaves correctly on normal data fails on malicious inputs. : adding small to a traffic sign to misinterpretation by an autonomous vehicle. is from a Prompt injection attack inputs manipulative instructions (instead of data) to make the model perform task incorrectly.
